players.product: diesel standby gensets (95 L / QSK95) and QSK60 / HSK78 natural gas gensets for data centers; 130 L natural gas prime-power genset in development

quarterly_data.signal: Record second quarter sales of $9.5 billion, up 9%, 'driven primarily by higher global demand in power generation markets, particularly from data centers'; record EBITDA of $1.7 billion or 17.5% of sales; operating cash flow a Q2 record $1.5 billion.

Power Systems segment revenue a record $2.3 billion, up 19%, EBITDA margin up to 24.5% from 22.8%; North America Power Systems revenue +19% on continued strong data center demand supported by capacity brought online at the end of 2025; China power generation equipment sales +88% on accelerating data center demand; China revenue $2.3 billion (+30%).
quarterly_data.figure: Power Systems revenue $2.3 billion (+19%), EBITDA 24.5%; China power gen +88%

quarterly_data.signal: Signed a multi-year agreement with a Global Hyperscaler (an existing customer), 'expanding a long-standing partnership and securing visibility into several gigawatts of future backup power genset demand'; backlog 'very strong' with customers asking 'how much more can we deliver'; demand for backup power 'is ahead of industry supply availability'.
quarterly_data.figure: several gigawatts of backup genset demand under multi-year hyperscaler agreement

quarterly_data.signal: Prime power entry: agreement with Circe Energy to provide QSK60 and HSK78 natural gas generator sets and integrated microgrid technology for a behind-the-meter prime power solution supporting a high-performance computing data center in Texas; developing a 130 L natural gas genset to extend into prime power, with Power Systems investment stepping up in the second half for that platform.

Capacity: 2026 power generation growth 'will continue to be constrained by capacity'; 20 GW of incremental capacity announced at the May Analyst Day across plants and supply chain — some online in 2027, a bigger step-up in 2028, phasing through 2030; large gensets are 'basically at capacity' so customers are taking smaller gensets; new orders now selling out into the second half of 2028 with 'absolutely no pausing or blinking in demand'.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 GW incremental capacity by 2030; large gensets sold out into 2H 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Raised 2026 outlook: total revenue +10%-13% (prior 8%-11%), EBITDA 18%-18.5%; global power generation revenues still expected +15%-25%; Power Systems revenue +14%-19% with EBITDA 25%-25.75%; capital investments $1.35 billion-$1.45 billion.

Mix outlook: 'the predominant revenue for PowerGen this decade is going to be diesel standby' even as natural gas prime demand begins; 2027 PowerGen capacity guidance deferred to later in the year ('it'll be high'); Analyst Day raised 2030 financial targets.
